tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

You are an expert code reviewer specializing in modern software development across multiple languages and frameworks. Your primary responsibility is to review code against project guidelines in CLAUDE.md with high precision to minimize false positives.

## Review Scope

By default, review unstaged changes from `git diff`. The user may specify different files or scope to review.

When assigned by geeky-orchestration, the review layer controls the scope:

- **Task:** answer whether the task meets its ACs and passes its defined tests. Confirm that the evidence demonstrates the required outcome within this review scope; successful execution alone is insufficient. Return an AC mapping, test evidence and PASS or NEEDS FIXES. Identify the specific unproved requirement before requesting more work; missing required evidence cannot pass. Acceptance must wait until all required tests have passing evidence, even when the task is not in the Blocked lane. An allowed retry permits remediation, not acceptance or dependent phase advancement. Inspect supporting contracts as needed without reopening the full implementation chain or adding acceptance requirements.
- **Phase:** in the same dispatch as the task reviews, assess the complete phase requirements and cross-task behavior. Use the task verdicts and evidence; conclude READY TO ADVANCE or BLOCKED with the unmet requirement or dependency.
- **Final:** follow the assigned `impl-review` domain and criteria.

Each blocking finding must identify the violated AC, defined test or existing mandatory constraint, concrete evidence, and the smallest correction. Severity alone does not expand the assignment. Optional hardening belongs in follow-ups.

Return a consolidated finding set within that contract. Route unrelated findings separately; they block only when they prevent the current contract from being met or make acceptance unsafe under an existing requirement. These boundaries govern the responsibilities below.

In a phase review, return a separate AC/test verdict for each task alongside the phase verdict; the tasks stay In Review until the review clears. Remain read-only. On re-review, assess only the affected tasks and preserve unaffected evidence.

## Core Review Responsibilities

**Project Guidelines Compliance**: Verify adherence to explicit project rules (typically in CLAUDE.md or equivalent) including import patterns, framework conventions, language-specific style, function declarations, error handling, logging, testing practices, platform compatibility, and naming conventions.

**Bug Detection**: Identify actual bugs that will impact functionality - logic errors, null/undefined handling, race conditions, memory leaks, security vulnerabilities, and performance problems.

**Code Quality**: Evaluate significant issues like code duplication, missing critical error handling, accessibility problems, and inadequate test coverage.

## Confidence Scoring

Rate each potential issue on a scale from 0-100:

- **0**: Not confident at all. This is a false positive that doesn't stand up to scrutiny, or is a pre-existing issue.
- **25**: Somewhat confident. This might be a real issue, but may also be a false positive. If stylistic, it wasn't explicitly called out in project guidelines.
- **50**: Moderately confident. This is a real issue, but might be a nitpick or not happen often in practice. Not very important relative to the rest of the changes.
- **75**: Highly confident. Double-checked and verified this is very likely a real issue that will be hit in practice. The existing approach is insufficient. Important and will directly impact functionality, or is directly mentioned in project guidelines.
- **100**: Absolutely certain. Confirmed this is definitely a real issue that will happen frequently in practice. The evidence directly confirms this.

**Only report issues with confidence ≥ 80.** Focus on issues that truly matter - quality over quantity.

Start by clearly stating what you're reviewing. For each high-confidence issue, provide:

- Clear description with confidence score
- File path and line number
- Specific project guideline reference or bug explanation
- Concrete fix suggestion

Structure your response for maximum actionability - developers should know exactly what to fix and why.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. 12	
13	```
14	linkvault/clock.py
15	  parse_ts(s: str) -> int          # strict YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, raises ValueError
16	  format_ts(n: int) -> str
17	  class Clock:  Clock(fake_start: int | None = None); .fake (bool); .now() -> int; .set(n: int)

19	linkvault/store.py
20	  hash_token(token: str) -> str    # sha256 hex
21	  class Store:  Store(path)        # connects, runs exact schema; raises sqlite3.Error/OSError
22	    .close()
23	    .add_token(token_hash, created_at)
24	    .token_exists(token_hash) -> bool
25	    .create_link(slug, url, token_hash, created_at, expires_at) -> bool   # False if slug exists

77	|---|---|---|---|

88	## 5. Cross-cutting rules
89	
90	- Request pipeline is linear and returns on first failure: route 404 -> auth 401 -> rate limit 429 -> size 413 -> JSON 400 -> validation 400 -> state 404/409/410. Read `now` once per request.
91	- Never write to stdout except the ready line; logs and tracebacks go to stderr.
92	- Every response sets `Content-Length`; JSON via `json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)`; no `sort_keys`.

28	- Handler: `protocol_version = "HTTP/1.0"` (D3); every response sets `Content-Length` (`0` for 204/302). Define `do_GET/POST/DELETE/PUT/PATCH/HEAD/OPTIONS` all routing to one dispatcher so unlisted pairs get 404 `not_found` JSON (not http.server's 501 HTML); override `send_error` to JSON and `log_message` to stderr. Nothing to stdout.
29	- Server: `ThreadingHTTPServer` on `("127.0.0.1", port)`, `daemon_threads = True`, `request_queue_size = 128`, `allow_reuse_address = False` on `win32`. `.port = server_address[1]`.
30	- Path: `self.path.split("?", 1)[0]`; no percent-decoding or trailing-slash normalisation. Slug routes (E5/E6/E7) use `re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}", slug)`; a failed match is a route miss -> 404 before auth. `GET /healthz` matches before the E7 slug route. E8 route exists only when the server has a fake clock, else 404 at route step.
31	- Pipeline (first failure wins): route -> auth -> rate limit -> size -> JSON -> validation -> state. Compute `now = clock.now()` once per request.
32	- Auth: admin routes compare `X-Admin-Key` with `hmac.compare_digest` on bytes (`.encode("utf-8","surrogateescape")` both sides; never on `str`); missing/wrong -> 401 `unauthorized`. Bearer routes: header must be exactly `Bearer <token>` (case-sensitive scheme, single space, D2), token matching `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`, `store.token_exists(hash_token(token))`; else 401.
33	- `RateLimiter(limit).hit(token_hash, now)`: dict `token_hash -> (window_start, count)` under a lock; `window_start = now - now % 60`; window change resets; returns `None` while `count <= limit`, else `window_start + 60 - now`. Applied only after successful bearer auth on link routes; counts every request reaching it (any final status). Exempt: E1, E2, E7, E8. 429 body code `rate_limited` plus `Retry-After` header.
34	- Size step (all routes after auth/rate limit): no `Content-Length` = empty body; non-numeric/negative -> 400 `invalid_request` + `Connection: close` (D4); `> 8192` -> 413 `payload_too_large` + `Connection: close`, body NOT read; else read exactly N bytes. JSON step only for routes that consume a body (E3, E8): invalid UTF-8 / invalid JSON / non-object -> 400 `invalid_json`; E2 ignores the body entirely.
35	- E2: token = `"lv_" + secrets.token_hex(16)`; `store.add_token(hash_token(token), now)`; 201 `{"token":..., "created_at":...}` in that key order. E8: `parse_clock_request` (ValidationError -> 400 `invalid_request`), `clock.set`, 200 `{"now":"<normalised ts>"}`.
36	- JSON encoding: `json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` UTF-8, `Content-Type: application/json`; never `sort_keys`. Error shape `{"error":{"code":..,"message":..}}`. Wrap the dispatcher in `try/except Exception` -> stderr traceback + 500 `internal`.
37	- JSON step: `body.decode("utf-8")` (strict) first, then `json.loads(str)`; `UnicodeDecodeError`, `ValueError` and `RecursionError` -> `invalid_json` (`json.loads(bytes)` would accept UTF-16/32).
38	- Size step applies to EVERY matched route including E1 and E7 (D8 uniform; the contract's 413 row is unconditional).
39	- Responses sent without consuming the body (401/404/429 etc.; not the 413 or bad-Content-Length paths) do a best-effort drain: only when `0 < Content-Length <= 8192`, read at most that many bytes with a ~0.2 s socket timeout, swallow timeout/reset errors, then ALWAYS send the response. Never drain when `Content-Length > 8192`; 413 never reads the body. Restore the normal socket timeout afterwards. Tests that expect 401/429/413 for a large declared body send headers only.
40	- `make_server`: if bind fails after the Store was opened, close the Store and re-raise. `fake_clock` parameter is an int epoch-second or None.
41	- A rate-limit window "change" includes a clock moved backwards into an earlier window (counter resets).
42	- Link routes E3-E6 are registered with stub handlers in T4 (500 `internal`) so the 429/`Retry-After` HTTP test can run on stub `GET /v1/links` (the stub's responses still count). That test asserts only `status != 429` for requests 1..N and 429 + `Retry-After` for request N+1 (never `== 500`), so it keeps passing when T5 replaces the stubs. No other T4 test may hard-code 500 for link routes.

49	* `POST /v1/tokens` with the right key -> 201, token matches `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`, keys `token,created_at` in order, `created_at` is the clock's timestamp; DB holds only its SHA-256; wrong/missing key -> 401 `unauthorized`.

1	# linkvault: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, stdlib only (`http.server`, `sqlite3`, `json`, `argparse`, `urllib`, `secrets`, `hashlib`, `threading`, `signal`); pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `linkvault/` at the workspace root (`linkvault/__init__.py`, `linkvault/__main__.py`); commands run with the workspace root as cwd.
7	- **Entry points:** `python -m linkvault serve ...` (server); `python -m linkvault <client-cmd> ...` (client).
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1 Server start.** `serve` opens or creates the DB, binds 127.0.0.1, then prints exactly one ready line to stdout. Nothing else is ever written to stdout; logs go to stderr.
12	- **R2 Token issuance.** `POST /v1/tokens` with the correct admin key returns a new token. The token is `lv_` followed by 32 lowercase hex characters (`secrets.token_hex(16)`). Only its SHA-256 hex digest is stored.
13	- **R3 Authentication.** Every `/v1/links` route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A missing, malformed or unknown token returns 401.
14	- **R4 Create link.** `POST /v1/links` stores `url` with a custom `slug` or a generated slug, and an optional `expires_in`.
15	- **R5 Slug rules.** Slugs are case-sensitive. A custom slug must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` and must not be `healthz`. A generated slug is 7 characters from `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789`, drawn with `secrets.choice`. It is regenerated if it already exists or is reserved, with up to 5 attempts and then 500. Creating an existing slug returns 409.
16	- **R6 URL rules.** The scheme is `http` or `https` (case-insensitive). `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname` is non-empty. The URL is at most 2048 characters and contains no whitespace or control characters (code points < 0x21 or 0x7F). It is stored and redirected to verbatim.
17	- **R7 Resolve.** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with `Location: <url>` and an empty body. It atomically increments `clicks` and sets `last_clicked_at` to now.
18	- **R8 Missing and expired links.** An unknown slug returns 404. A link with `now >= expires_at` returns 410 and its click count is unchanged. Comparisons use whole seconds.
19	- **R9 List and inspect.** A token can list its own links (expired ones included) and fetch one link with its stats. Another token's link always returns 404, never 403.
20	- **R10 Delete.** A token can delete its own link. Afterwards the slug resolves 404 and is free to reuse.
21	- **R11 Rate limit.** Requests are counted per token in fixed 60-second windows aligned to the Unix epoch (`window_start = now - now % 60`). The limit is `--rate-limit` (default 60) counted requests per window. A request is counted when it reaches the rate-limit step (see precedence in Error handling), whatever its final status. Request number `limit + 1` and later in the same window return 429 with `Retry-After: <window_start + 60 - now>`. Counters are in memory and reset on restart. Redirects, `/healthz` and admin routes are not rate-limited.
22	- **R12 Clock.** "Now" is integer Unix seconds (floor of real time). With `--fake-clock <ISO>`, now is frozen at that instant and changes only through `POST /v1/admin/clock`. The fake clock is not persisted.
23	- **R13 Persistence.** Tokens, links, clicks and `last_clicked_at` survive a restart on the same `--db`.
24	- **R14 Concurrency.** The server is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`. N concurrent redirects to one slug leave `clicks == N` exactly.
25	- **R15 Shutdown.** On SIGINT, SIGTERM (POSIX) or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT/SIGBREAK (Windows), the server stops accepting connections, closes the DB and exits 0 within 5 seconds.
26	- **R16 Client.** CLI commands wrap the API. Each prints the response body to stdout, and uses the exit codes below.
27	
28	## Interface contract
29	
30	### Conventions
31	
32	- Timestamps are `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC with whole seconds. They are stored as INTEGER Unix seconds.
33	- JSON responses are encoded with `json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` in UTF-8, with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every response sets `Content-Length`; a 204 response has an empty body and MUST send `Content-Length: 0`. Keys appear in exactly the order listed below.
34	- Request `Content-Type` is ignored. The body is read using `Content-Length` (absent means empty), and the maximum is 8192 bytes.
35	- Query strings are ignored on every route. Paths are matched exactly, with no trailing-slash normalisation. Any (method, path) pair not listed below returns 404 `not_found`.
36	- `short_url` is `http://127.0.0.1:<bound port>/<slug>`.
37	
38	**Link object** (key order is fixed): `{"slug", "url", "short_url", "created_at", "expires_at", "clicks", "last_clicked_at"}`. `expires_at` and `last_clicked_at` are `null` until they are set.
39	
40	### Server CLI
41	
42	```
43	python -m linkvault serve --db PATH --admin-key KEY [--port N] [--rate-limit N] [--fake-clock ISO]
44	```
45	
46	| Flag | Rule |
47	|---|---|
48	| `--db` | Required. The file is created if missing, and its parent directory must exist. |
49	| `--admin-key` | Required. Non-empty string. |
50	| `--port` | 0-65535, default 8000. The value 0 binds an OS-chosen free port. |
51	| `--rate-limit` | Integer >= 1, default 60. |
52	| `--fake-clock` | An ISO timestamp in the format above. It enables the admin clock route. |
53	
54	Ready line: `LISTENING http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by a line terminator, which may be `\n` or `\r\n`. It uses the actual bound port, is flushed immediately, and nothing else is written to stdout before it.
55	
56	Exit codes: 0 for a clean shutdown; 2 for a usage error (argparse); 3 if the port cannot be bound or the DB cannot be opened, with a message to stderr.
57	
58	### Endpoints
59	
60	| # | Method and path | Auth | Request body | Success response |
61	|---|---|---|---|---|
62	| E1 | `GET /healthz` | none | none | 200 `{"status":"ok"}` |
63	| E2 | `POST /v1/tokens` | `X-Admin-Key: <key>` | ignored | 201 `{"token":"lv_…","created_at":"…"}` |
64	| E3 | `POST /v1/links` | Bearer | `{"url": str, "slug"?: str, "expires_in"?: int}` | 201, link object |
65	| E4 | `GET /v1/links` | Bearer | none | 200 `{"links":[link…]}` ordered by `created_at` ascending, then `slug` ascending |
66	| E5 | `GET /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 200, link object |
67	| E6 | `DELETE /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 204, empty body |
68	| E7 | `GET /<slug>` | none | none | 302, `Location: <url>`, `Content-Length: 0`, empty body |
69	| E8 | `POST /v1/admin/clock` | `X-Admin-Key` | `{"now": ISO}` | 200 `{"now":"…"}`. The route exists only with `--fake-clock`; otherwise it returns 404. Any valid timestamp is accepted. |
70	
71	E3 body rules:
72	- The body is a JSON object with no extra keys.
73	- `url` is required and must follow R6.
74	- `slug` is optional and must follow R5. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400).
75	- `expires_in` is optional. It is an integer from 1 to 31536000, and `bool` values are rejected. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400). It sets `expires_at = created_at + expires_in`.
76	
77	E8 body rules:
78	- The body must be exactly `{"now": ISO}`, where ISO is a string in the timestamp format above.
79	- A missing `now` key, an extra key, a wrong type or an unparseable timestamp returns 400 `invalid_request`.
80	
81	A wrong or missing admin key on E2 or E8 returns 401. On E5, E6 and E7, a `<slug>` that fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` is a route mismatch, so it returns 404 at the route step, before auth.
82	
83	### DB schema (exact)
84	
85	```sql
86	PRAGMA user_version = 1;
87	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
88	  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
89	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
90	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
91	  slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
92	  url TEXT NOT NULL,
93	  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tokens(token_hash),
94	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
95	  expires_at INTEGER,
96	  clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
97	  last_clicked_at INTEGER);
98	```
99	
100	A click is recorded with one statement: `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?`.
101	
102	### Client CLI
103	
104	The server URL comes from `--server URL`, or else the `LINKVAULT_SERVER` environment variable. The token comes from `--token T`, or else `LINKVAULT_TOKEN`. Both options are accepted after the subcommand.
105	
106	| Command | Calls | Stdout on success |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| `token create --admin-key K` | E2 | Response JSON, one line |
109	| `shorten URL [--slug S] [--expires-in N]` | E3 | Response JSON, one line |
110	| `list` | E4 | Response JSON, one line |
111	| `stats SLUG` | E5 | Response JSON, one line |
112	| `delete SLUG` | E6 | Nothing |
113	
114	Output is re-serialised with the server's `json.dumps` settings and ends with `\n`. Client exit codes:
115	
116	| Code | Meaning | Output |
117	|---|---|---|
118	| 0 | 2xx response | as above |
119	| 1 | non-2xx response | Error JSON on stderr, stdout empty |
120	| 2 | usage error, or a missing server or token | Message on stderr |
121	| 3 | connection failure | Message on stderr |
122	
123	## Error handling
124	
125	Every error body has this shape: `{"error":{"code":"<code>","message":"<text>"}}`. Tests assert `code` only.
126	
127	| Condition | Status | code |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| No route matches the method and path; unknown or foreign slug | 404 | `not_found` |
130	| Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token; bad admin key | 401 | `unauthorized` |
131	| Over the rate limit (adds a `Retry-After` header) | 429 | `rate_limited` |
132	| `Content-Length` > 8192 (the response sets `Connection: close` and the body is not read) | 413 | `payload_too_large` |
133	| Body is not valid UTF-8 JSON, or is not an object | 400 | `invalid_json` |
134	| Schema violation: missing or extra key, wrong type, bad URL, slug, `expires_in` or `now` | 400 | `invalid_request` |
135	| Slug already exists, or is reserved (`healthz`) | 409 | `slug_taken` |
136	| Link expired (E7 only) | 410 | `gone` |
137	| Unhandled exception | 500 | `internal` |
138	
139	Precedence (first failure wins): route 404 → auth 401 → rate limit 429 → size 413 → JSON 400 → validation 400 → resource state 404/409/410.
140	
141	## Acceptance criteria
142	
143	- **AC1 (R1, R15):** `serve --port 0` prints exactly the `LISTENING` line. `GET /healthz` returns 200. SIGINT (or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows) makes it exit 0 within 5 s.
144	- **AC2 (R2):** E2 with the right key returns 201 and a token matching `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`. With a wrong key it returns 401. The DB holds the SHA-256 of the token, never the plaintext.
145	- **AC3 (R3):** E3, E4 and E5 without a valid bearer token return 401 `unauthorized`.
146	- **AC4 (R4, R5):** E3 without `slug` returns a slug matching `^[a-z0-9]{7}$`. A custom `slug` is echoed back. A repeated slug returns 409. `healthz` and `ab` return 409 and 400 respectively.
147	- **AC5 (R6):** `ftp://x`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `http://`, a URL with a space, and a 2049-character URL each return 400 `invalid_request`.
148	- **AC6 (R7):** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with the exact `Location`. A later E5 shows `clicks` 1 and `last_clicked_at` set to now.
149	- **AC7 (R8, R12):** With the fake clock at T and `expires_in=60`, the link resolves 302 at T+59 and 410 at T+60. Its clicks stay at the T+59 value.
150	- **AC8 (R9, R10):** Token B gets 404 on E5 and E6 for token A's slug. A's E4 lists only A's links in order. After E6, `GET /<slug>` returns 404 and the slug can be created again.
151	- **AC9 (R11):** With `--rate-limit 3` and the fake clock at a window start plus 10 s, requests 1-3 succeed. Request 4 returns 429 with `Retry-After: 50`. After the clock moves to the next window, the next request succeeds. Redirects are never limited.
152	- **AC10 (R13):** After a restart on the same DB, tokens still authenticate, and links and clicks are unchanged.
153	- **AC11 (R14):** 50 concurrent `GET /<slug>` requests leave `clicks == 50`.
154	- **AC12 (R16):** `shorten` prints the link JSON and exits 0. A 409 makes it exit 1 with empty stdout. An unreachable server makes it exit 3. A missing token makes it exit 2.

12	
13	## 1. Executive Summary
14	
15	Build `linkvault`, a small URL-shortener HTTP JSON API plus command-line client, in the `linkvault/` package at the repo root. Stdlib only (`http.server`, `sqlite3`, `json`, `argparse`, `urllib`, `secrets`, `hashlib`, `threading`, `signal`); pytest for tests only. An admin key issues bearer tokens; each token manages only its own links; links redirect with 302, may carry a custom slug and an expiry, and count clicks. Tokens are rate-limited with in-memory fixed windows; everything else persists in SQLite. The server binds 127.0.0.1, prints one `LISTENING` line, supports a fake clock, and shuts down cleanly on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGBREAK. An automated suite checks status codes, JSON keys and order, headers, output and exit codes.

17	## 2. Problem Statement
18

20	The repository contains only `brief.md`, `contract.md` and `.gitignore` (one commit, `0f18acb seed: brief and contract`). There is no code, no tests, no `docs/` history, no `CLAUDE.md`.

25	## 3. Goals & Non-Goals

27	**Goals**

35	## 4. Architecture
36	
37	```
38	linkvault/
39	  __init__.py     version only
40	  __main__.py     argparse: `serve` + client subcommands, dispatch, exit codes
41	  clock.py        real/fake clock, strict timestamp parse/format
42	  validate.py     pure slug/URL/body validators
43	  store.py        sqlite3 wrapper (one connection + one lock): schema, tokens, links, click

51	Modules may be merged where it keeps the code smaller (for example the rate limiter lives in `server.py`). Run all commands with the workspace root as cwd.
52	
53	Data flow per request: the handler computes `now` once, then runs a linear pipeline that returns on the first failure:
54	route (404) -> auth (401) -> rate limit (429) -> size (413) -> JSON (400 `invalid_json`) -> validation (400 `invalid_request`) -> resource state (404/409/410) -> success.
55	
56	## 5. Detailed Design
57	
58	### 5.1 Environment and interpreter compatibility (decision)
59	The contract requires Python >= 3.11. The only interpreter verified to run in the build environment is Python 3.9.6 (`python3`, with pytest 8.4.2); `/usr/local/bin/python3` (3.14) is killed with exit 137 in the sandbox. **Decision:** write code that is valid on 3.9 and 3.11+ so it is testable here: add `from __future__ import annotations` in modules that use `X | None` annotations, and avoid `match`, `datetime.UTC`, `datetime.fromisoformat` on `Z` strings, `sqlite3` `autocommit=`, `tomllib`, `StrEnum` and `typing.Self`. Test evidence must state the interpreter version used.
60	
61	### 5.2 Clock (R12)
62	- `now()` is `int(time.time())` or, with `--fake-clock`, a frozen integer guarded by a lock and changed only by E8.
63	- Timestamp format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. Parse strictly: `re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z", s)` first (`strptime` alone accepts `2026-1-1T0:0:0Z`), then `datetime.datetime(y, mo, d, h, mi, s)` (raises `ValueError` for impossible dates), then `calendar.timegm`. Format from `datetime.datetime(1970,1,1) + datetime.timedelta(seconds=n)` fields with an f-string (`%04d-%02d-%02dT%02d:%02d:%02dZ`); not `strftime("%Y")` (glibc does not zero-pad years < 1000) and not `time.gmtime` (negative values fail on Windows).
64	- An invalid `--fake-clock` value is a usage error (exit 2) via an argparse `type` function.
65	
66	### 5.3 Store (R2, R4, R7-R10, R13, R14)
67	- One `sqlite3.connect(path, check_same_thread=False, isolation_level=None)` (autocommit) and one `threading.Lock` around every operation.
68	- On start run `executescript` with the exact schema from the contract (`PRAGMA user_version = 1;` plus the two `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`). Foreign keys stay off; no WAL.
69	- Tokens: store only `hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest()`.
70	- Create link: `INSERT` and catch `sqlite3.IntegrityError` -> 409 `slug_taken` (no check-then-insert race).
71	- Resolve: inside the lock, `SELECT url, expires_at`; unknown -> 404; `expires_at is not None and now >= expires_at` -> 410 with no click; else run the exact contract statement `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?` and return the URL.
72	- List: `ORDER BY created_at ASC, slug ASC`, only the caller's `token_hash`, expired included. Inspect and delete are scoped by `slug AND token_hash`; a foreign or unknown slug is 404 (never 403). Delete frees the slug.
73	- Opening failures (`sqlite3.Error`, `OSError`) include a missing parent directory and a non-database file (the latter surfaces at the first statement, so connect and schema setup are wrapped together).
74	
75	### 5.4 Server (R1, R3, R5-R8, R11, R14, R15)
76	- `ThreadingHTTPServer` bound to `("127.0.0.1", port)`; `daemon_threads = True`; `request_queue_size = 128` (AC11 bursts 50 connects); `allow_reuse_address = False` on `win32`. The bound port is `server.server_address[1]` and is used for `short_url` and the ready line.
77	- Handler `protocol_version = "HTTP/1.0"` (**decision**): the connection closes after each response, so unread request bodies cannot corrupt a following request and keep-alive connections cannot delay shutdown. Every response still sets `Content-Length` (including `0` for 204 and 302) and the 413 response additionally sets `Connection: close`.
78	- Define `do_GET`, `do_POST`, `do_DELETE`, `do_PUT`, `do_PATCH`, `do_HEAD`, `do_OPTIONS`, all funnelled into one dispatcher, so every unlisted (method, path) pair gets 404 `not_found` JSON instead of `http.server`'s 501 HTML. Override `send_error` to emit the JSON error shape, and `log_message` to write to stderr. Nothing but the ready line is ever written to stdout.
79	- **Routing:** strip the query with `self.path.split("?", 1)[0]` (not `urlsplit`, which treats `//x/y` as a netloc); no percent-decoding; no trailing-slash normalisation. Slug-bearing routes (E5, E6, E7) use `re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}", slug)` (ASCII class; `re.match` with `$` would accept a trailing newline); a non-matching slug is a route miss (404) before auth. Match `GET /healthz` (E1) before E7. E8 exists only with `--fake-clock`, otherwise 404 at the route step.
80	- **Auth:** E2 and E8 compare `X-Admin-Key` using `hmac.compare_digest` on bytes (both sides `.encode("utf-8", "surrogateescape")`; never on `str`, which raises `TypeError` for non-ASCII); missing or wrong -> 401. E3-E6 require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: exactly the scheme `Bearer` (case-sensitive, **decision**: the contract writes it literally), one space, then a token matching `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`, whose SHA-256 must exist in `tokens`. Anything else -> 401 `unauthorized`.
81	- **Rate limit (R11):** a dict `token_hash -> (window_start, count)` under one lock. `now` is read once per request; `window_start = now - now % 60`; a changed window resets the count. Applies only to authenticated E3-E6 requests, counted when they reach the rate-limit step regardless of final status (so 400, 404, 409 and 413 count; 401 and route misses do not). Count `> limit` -> 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After: window_start + 60 - now`. E1, E2, E7 and E8 are exempt.
82	- **Size/body:** the size step runs for every route that passes auth/rate limiting (including routes that ignore bodies). Absent `Content-Length` means an empty body. `Content-Length > 8192` -> 413 `payload_too_large` with `Connection: close`, body unread. A non-numeric or negative `Content-Length` -> 400 `invalid_request` with `Connection: close` (**decision**; the contract is silent). Otherwise read exactly that many bytes.
83	- **JSON step (E3, E8 only; E2 ignores its body):** the body must decode as UTF-8 JSON and be an object, otherwise 400 `invalid_json` (an empty body is `invalid_json`).
84	- **E3 validation (400 `invalid_request`):** no extra keys; `url` required and a `str`; `slug` optional, `str`, must match the slug regex, an explicit `null` is rejected; `expires_in` optional, `int` (reject `bool` explicitly; floats such as `60.0` are rejected), 1..31536000, explicit `null` rejected. `healthz` passes the regex and is rejected at the state step as 409 (`ab` is 400).
85	- **URL validation order (R6), on the raw string:** `str` -> `len(url) <= 2048` (code points) -> no code point `< 0x21` or `== 0x7F` (this must run before `urlsplit`, which silently strips tab/CR/LF) -> encodable as UTF-8 (a lone surrogate from a JSON `\ud800` escape would otherwise crash SQLite; reject as 400) -> `try: urlsplit(url) except ValueError` -> 400 -> `scheme in ("http","https")` (`urlsplit` lowercases the scheme) -> `hostname` truthy. The port is never inspected; non-ASCII hosts and paths are accepted. The URL is stored verbatim.
86	- **Generated slug (R5):** 7 characters of `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789` via `secrets.choice`; up to 5 attempts, retrying on existing or reserved (`healthz`); then 500 `internal`.
87	- **Redirect (R7):** 302, `Location` verbatim, `Content-Length: 0`, empty body. Because `send_header` encodes as latin-1, emit the header value as `url.encode("utf-8").decode("latin-1")` so non-ASCII URLs are sent as their UTF-8 bytes without raising (**decision**).
88	- **JSON output:** `json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` encoded UTF-8, `Content-Type: application/json`, dict insertion order, never `sort_keys`. 204 has an empty body and `Content-Length: 0` (this deliberately deviates from RFC 9110 section 8.6, which says a 204 must not carry `Content-Length`; the contract wins and `http.client`/`urllib` accept it).
89	- Wrap the dispatcher in `try/except Exception` -> log traceback to stderr, 500 `internal`.
90	- **Early-error body drain:** responses sent before the body was consumed (401/404/429 etc.) do a best-effort drain only when `0 < Content-Length <= 8192` (short ~0.2 s socket timeout, errors swallowed, response always sent) to avoid TCP resets; never when `Content-Length > 8192`; 413 never reads the body.
91	- **Serve and shutdown (R1, R15):** open the DB first, then bind; on `sqlite3.Error`/`OSError` from either, write a message to stderr, release what was opened, and exit 3. Once both succeeded, install handlers for `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM` and (when `hasattr(signal, "SIGBREAK")`) `SIGBREAK` BEFORE printing the ready line, so a signal right after the ready line cannot hit Python's default handler (exit 130). Then print `LISTENING http://127.0.0.1:<port>` with `print(..., flush=True)` and call `serve_forever(poll_interval=0.1)` on the main thread. The handler must not call `shutdown()` on the serving thread (deadlock): it starts a daemon thread running `server.shutdown()`. After `serve_forever` returns: `server_close()`, take the store lock, close the DB, exit 0.
92	- **Server CLI validation (argparse, exit 2):** `--db` and `--admin-key` required; `--admin-key` non-empty; `--port` integer 0-65535 default 8000; `--rate-limit` integer >= 1 default 60; `--fake-clock` strict timestamp.
93	
94	### 5.5 Client (R16)
95	- `python -m linkvault token create --admin-key K`, `shorten URL [--slug S] [--expires-in N]`, `list`, `stats SLUG`, `delete SLUG`. `--server` and `--token` are accepted after the subcommand (define them on each subparser, or on a shared parent parser, avoiding a top-level/sub-level default clobbering trap) and fall back to `LINKVAULT_SERVER` / `LINKVAULT_TOKEN`.
96	- Missing server, or missing token for every command except `token create`, is exit 2 with a stderr message, detected before any network call. A malformed server URL (`ValueError`) is also exit 2 (**decision**).
97	- Use `urllib.request` with an explicit timeout. 2xx: re-serialise the body with the server's `json.dumps` settings plus `\n` on stdout (nothing for `delete`'s 204), exit 0. `HTTPError` (caught before `URLError`, its superclass): error JSON on stderr, stdout empty, exit 1. Connection failures (`URLError`, `OSError`, `TimeoutError`, `http.client.HTTPException`): message on stderr, exit 3. Argparse errors: exit 2.
98	
99	### 5.6 Test strategy
100	- Integration tests start `python -m linkvault serve --port 0 --db <tmp> --admin-key k [--fake-clock ...]` as a subprocess with the repo root as cwd, read the `LISTENING` line with a timeout (regex `^LISTENING http://127\.0\.0\.1:(\d+)\r?\n$`), drain stderr, and always terminate it in teardown. Requests use `http.client` (never `urllib`, which follows 302s). Windows variants use `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` and `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT`; POSIX uses `send_signal(SIGINT/SIGTERM)` and `wait(timeout=5)`.
101	- Cover every AC plus the traps: bool/null `expires_in`, null `slug`, `healthz` 409 vs `ab` 400, bad slug 404 before auth, `Retry-After: 50`, expiry boundary T+59/T+60 with unchanged clicks, foreign-slug 404 on E5 and E6, delete then recreate, 413 without sending the oversize body, rate-limit counting of non-success requests, 50 concurrent redirects giving `clicks == 50`, restart persistence, stdout containing only the ready line, DB containing only the token hash, client exit codes 0/1/2/3, PUT/PATCH/HEAD/OPTIONS returning 404 JSON.
102

**Verdict: NEEDS FIXES.** There are no Critical findings. One Warning is a stale design statement left in the PM review file. The rest are Suggestions.

I had no shell tool, so I could not run `git diff`. I read the plan, spec, `contract.md`, and tasks T1, T4, T5, T6, T7, T8, T9, plus draft, kanban, references, README, handoff and the PM review file, and grepped the whole folder.

## Earlier findings: resolved and consistent
- **C1 (early-error drain vs headers-only tests):** The new wording is identical in `implementation-plan.md` §5 (line 96), `feature-specification.md` §5.4 (line 90) and `tasks/T4-http-core-admin-routes.md` (line 39).
  - Rule: drain only when `0 < Content-Length <= 8192`, about 0.2 s timeout, errors swallowed, response always sent.
  - Never drain above 8192, and 413 never reads the body.
  - T4's timing tests (`Content-Length: 9000` returns in under 1 s, `Content-Length: 100` in under 2 s) hold under this rule.
  - T5 line 44 tests D8 on E7 with headers only.
  - A grep for `timeout = 5` and "5 s" finds only the R15 shutdown deadline and the test `wait(timeout=5)`. No active spec, plan or task document says a 5 s drain.
- **Stale text:** T1 `pytest.ini` and the `format_ts` fix (T1 line 29, spec line 63) agree. T1's stub `__main__` and T6's `serve` in `server.py` with `build_parser()` agree. I found no "or `__main__`" left. The `RecursionError` handling in T4 is fine.
- **Fixture interfaces:** `start_server` (with the `.base_url`, `.db_path`, `.proc`, `.stdout_lines` and `.stop(sig)` attributes and `creationflags`) and `run_serve` are in plan §2 and defined in T6 before T7 and T8 use them. `server_factory` is defined in T4 before T5 uses it.
- **T4 429 test:** It now asserts only `status != 429` for requests 1..N and 429 plus `Retry-After` for request N+1, and says no other T4 test may hard-code 500. This is achievable with the stub `GET /v1/links`.
- **T7:** The `dest` on both subparsers and `required=True` are in place. The T6 parser has a `serve` subcommand, so a no-argument run exits 2 in both T6 and T7.
- **Contract and sequencing:** I found no contradiction with `contract.md`. The 401, 429 and 413 precedence is untouched, 413 still does not read the body, and the shutdown deadline is 5 s. Dependencies are unchanged (T4 depends on T1–T3, T5 on T4, T6 on T5, T7 on T6, T8 on T7, T9 on T8). The T7 and T8 test-file lists are unchanged apart from the T6 entries.

## Findings

**Warning**
1. `docs/spec-001-feature/review-development-project-manager.md`, line 25, still records the superseded design: "bounded drain of `min(Content-Length, 8192)` bytes ... with a 5 s handler socket timeout". This contradicts the new rule, which never drains above 8192 and uses a 0.2 s timeout.
   - **Fix:** change it to "best-effort drain only when `0 < Content-Length <= 8192`, ~0.2 s timeout, never above 8192; 413 never reads the body".
2. Same file, line 30: "T1: build timestamps from `gmtime` fields". T1 now forbids `time.gmtime` and uses `datetime` plus timedelta arithmetic.
   - **Fix:** change it to "build from `datetime(1970,1,1)+timedelta` fields (not `strftime`, not `time.gmtime`)".

**Suggestion**
3. `tasks/T4-http-core-admin-routes.md`, line 53: "wrong admin key with a 9000-byte body is 401 not 413" is ambiguous. If an implementer actually sends 9000 bytes, the server closes with unread data, and the macOS TCP reset risk this edit was meant to avoid comes back. Reword to "`Content-Length: 9000`, headers only".
4. `tasks/T5-link-endpoints.md`, line 32 (precedence table): add "413 cases send headers only; no body". T4's rule at line 39 does not appear in T5, and "429 before 413" and "413 before invalid_json" are exactly where a body might be sent.
5. `tasks/T4-http-core-admin-routes.md`, line 61 (429 HTTP test): say it uses `server_factory(fake_clock=<window start + 10>)`. With the real clock, a 60 s window rollover mid-test can make it flaky, and the exact `Retry-After` value is only assertable with a fixed clock.
6. `tasks/T7-cli-client.md`, line 39: add a missing-subcommand case (`python -m linkvault` with no arguments, and `token` with no `create`) to the acceptance criteria. Right now it appears only in the technical note at line 29.
7. `tasks/T6-serve-command-shutdown.md`, line 13: give `run_serve` an explicit timeout, for example `subprocess.run(..., timeout=15)`, so a server that wrongly starts listening cannot hang the suite.
8. `tasks/T1-package-skeleton-clock.md`, line 29: `parse_ts` accepts year 9999, so after E8 `expires_at = now + expires_in` can overflow `format_ts` and return 500. This is an edge case the contract's "any valid timestamp" wording touches. Either note `OverflowError` -> an accepted limitation, or clamp.

No files were created or modified.
